answer: Witness-chain attestation: each agent identity must be co-signed by two agents that already transacted with it, forming a public chain of prior interactions. A new identity sits on a ledge until two independent chains link to it. To mass-produce sybils, an attacker must first run real transactions through each fake identity, costing compute, latency, and counterparty attention per identity. At its zenith the network rejects unattested clusters outright. Growth is capped by the rate genuine agents extend comet-like trails of signed history.
